claim.detail: The single three-column table (Category / Field name / Description) is fragmented into a plain-text header line, three separate two-column tables and loose paragraphs; mon_decimal_point, mon_thousands_sep and n_cs_precedes fall outside any table, and the p_cs_precedes description is cut, with 'a nonnegative quantity' detached as its own paragraph. The Category column association is lost.
claim.why_it_matters: The table that defines the locale fields the standard references is broken into fragments, so field-to-category association and some field rows are outside the table, and one description is cut mid-sentence.

verdict.reasoning: The printed page 87 (8.2.1) is a borderless, whitespace-aligned list: a bold header line 'Category / Field name / Description', the category LC_MONETARY on its own line followed by 11 indented field/description rows, then LC_TIME on its own line followed by d_fmt and t_fmt. The markdown carries every field name and every description word for word (int_curr_symbol, currency_symbol, mon_decimal_point, mon_thousands_sep, mon_grouping, positive_sign, negative_sign, int_frac_digits, frac_digits, p_cs_precedes, n_cs_precedes, d_fmt, t_fmt), in the printed order, each under the category heading it falls under on the page, so the category association is preserved by sequence exactly as the print conveys it. The p_cs_precedes description 'a nonnegative quantity' is the printed line wrap (the PDF also wraps it to a second line) and sits directly after its row. The differences are inconsistent table/paragraph markup and line wrapping; no text is missing, misquoted or changed in meaning.
verdict.corrected_description: Formatting only: the markdown renders the borderless 8.2.1 locale-field list as a mix of pipe tables and loose lines and splits the p_cs_precedes description at the printed line wrap; all content and its order (and so the category grouping) are intact.
